From 18d78171c061889a9a43152f60d6a27a10fc7656 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Ming Lei <ming.lei@redhat.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2021 17:07:16 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] blk-mq: check q->poll_stat in queue_poll_stat_show

Without checking q->poll_stat in queue_poll_stat_show(), kernel panic
may be caused if q->poll_stat isn't allocated.

Fixes: 48b5c1fbcd8c ("block: only allocate poll_stats if there's a user of them")
Signed-off-by: Ming Lei <ming.lei@redhat.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20211202090716.3292244-1-ming.lei@redhat.com
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>

diff --git a/block/blk-mq-debugfs.c b/block/blk-mq-debugfs.c
index 7f27dca3a45e..3a790eb4995c 100644
--- a/block/blk-mq-debugfs.c
+++ b/block/blk-mq-debugfs.c
@@ -30,6 +30,9 @@ static int queue_poll_stat_show(void *data, struct seq_file *m)
 	struct request_queue *q = data;
 	int bucket;
 
+	if (!q->poll_stat)
+		return 0;
+
 	for (bucket = 0; bucket < (BLK_MQ_POLL_STATS_BKTS / 2); bucket++) {
 		seq_printf(m, "read  (%d Bytes): ", 1 << (9 + bucket));
 		print_stat(m, &q->poll_stat[2 * bucket]);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `block/blk-mq-debugfs.c`**
   - A check was added at the beginning of the `queue_poll_stat_show` function to verify if `q->poll_stat` is allocated. If `q->poll_stat` is not allocated (i.e., it is NULL), the function will return 0 immediately, preventing any further processing.

### Relationships

- The modification addresses a potential kernel panic issue that could occur if `q->poll_stat` is accessed without being allocated. By adding this check, the patch ensures that the function can safely handle cases where `q->poll_stat` is not initialized, thus improving the stability of the kernel code related to block device polling statistics. The change is directly related to the fix for the bug introduced in commit `48b5c1fbcd8c`, which only allocates `poll_stat` when there is a user of it.

Here is the commit message:
blk-mq: check q->poll_stat in queue_poll_stat_show

Without checking q->poll_stat in queue_poll_stat_show(), kernel panic
may be caused if q->poll_stat isn't allocated.

Fixes: 48b5c1fbcd8c ("block: only allocate poll_stats if there's a user of them")
Signed-off-by: Ming Lei <ming.lei@redhat.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20211202090716.3292244-1-ming.lei@redhat.com
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs because the `queue_poll_stat_show` function attempts to access `q->poll_stat` without checking if it has been allocated. If `q->poll_stat` is NULL, this leads to dereferencing a null pointer, which can cause a kernel panic. The root cause is the lack of a safety check before accessing `q->poll_stat`, especially since `poll_stat` is only allocated when there is an actual user of it.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int queue_poll_stat_show(void *data, struct seq_file *m)
 {
 	struct request_queue *q = data;
 	int bucket;
 
+	if (!q->poll_stat)
+		return 0;
+
 	for (bucket = 0; bucket < (BLK_MQ_POLL_STATS_BKTS / 2); bucket++) {
 		seq_printf(m, "read  (%d Bytes): ", 1 << (9 + bucket));
 		print_stat(m, &q->poll_stat[2 * bucket]);
 		seq_puts(m, "\n");
 
 		seq_printf(m, "write (%d Bytes): ",  1 << (9 + bucket));
 		print_stat(m, &q->poll_stat[2 * bucket + 1]);
 		seq_puts(m, "\n");
 	}
 	return 0;
 }
